authority.ruling_verbatim: owner 层面放行：授权将该补丁的晋升流程启动，但 D1/D2/D3 的专业签字仍属他方（见 TIER-2）。未获该三方签字前仍禁止把 iso/slo_probe_patched.py 拷进 RF/tools/；I-16 实测前必须先提供 bundle 测量文件。
authority.nature: a HALF-authorisation: it GRANTS a permission (start the promotion process) and WITHHOLDS the three specialist signatures, while restating a standing ban

why_a_permission_cannot_be_checked_for_c: Authorising the START of a process is a permission, not an act. A permission leaves no artifact, so 'was it done?' is a category error. What can be verified is that the permission did not overreach: no artifact appeared, the withheld signatures are still withheld, the ban is registered, the ban is obeyed, and the pending-party rows were not rewritten to 'owner decided'.
the_failure_mode_this_card_exists_to_cat: Reading 'owner 层面放行' as if it lifted the ban or supplied the three signatures, and therefore promoting iso/slo_probe_patched.py into tools/slo_probe.py -- the concrete form of the batch rule that a general approval must not swell into all the individual conclusions.

deliverable.conclusion: the permission left no artifact; D1/D2/D3 are each still owned by the other party and no carrier reads as signed; the ban is on disk in four carriers and names RF/tools/; the ban is OBEYED (production tools/slo_probe.py is still the pre-patch content and the patched file exists only inside this attempt); and the TIER-2 rows still say pending-party. This card wrote nothing.
deliverable.why_no_write: the ruling orders no write. Both halves already hold on disk: the permission is inherently formless, and manufacturing an artifact for it would convert a permission into an act; the three signatures remain other parties' to give, so supplying them would be forgery.
deliverable.self_hash_note: handoff.json cannot register its own hash (self-reference); it registers the three artifacts above. Its own hash is recorded in task_plan.md and the memory log only.

error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.error: V-1 first run FAIL: the criterion equated 'a file whose name contains promot' with 'a promotion artifact', and matched an unrelated subsystem's portfolio_promoter.py. A name collision, not evidence.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.fixed_by: scoping the check to the promotion's actual destination in this repo (tools/slo_probe.py), not to filename keywords.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.lesson: a criterion must be defined by the object's destination, not by vocabulary that happens to appear in its name

error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.error: V-2 first run FAIL (four successive drafts): (1) per-line keyword grep flagged the PROHIBITION 'must not happen until D1 is signed'; (2) paragraph co-occurrence matched unrelated 'confirmed' clauses; (3) clause-level matching still hit 'Signer:', 'fails closed', 'the D2 signature'; (4) including 'accepted' as a signature verb hit 'is not self-accepted' and the em-dash split defeated the negation guard.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.fixed_by: testing the SIGNEDNESS PREDICATE (state verb bound to a D-label) instead of the vocabulary of signing, and explicitly excluding the lexical traps; 'accepted' removed because in this corpus it means the reviewer's accepted_scoped verdict, a different predicate.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.lesson: the words 'sign', 'signer', 'signature', 'closed' all appear in text that does NOT claim signedness. Test the predicate, not the vocabulary.

error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.error: V-4 first run FAIL -- and this one nearly produced the OPPOSITE of the truth. Raw byte sha256 said production != pre-patch, i.e. 'the patch WAS promoted'.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.fixed_by: recognising that iso/ is CRLF and production is LF so the two are byte-different but content-identical; comparing content (newline-normalised) and recording the newline-only difference explicitly.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.lesson: the comparison surface must match the question asked. 'Is this file that file' is about CONTENT. Byte hashing can systematically invert the answer in a repo with core.autocrlf=true -- this is the 6th occurrence of this family here.

error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.error: V-5 first run FAIL: the TIER-2 preamble reads '本类不得记为 owner 已裁' -- the prohibition itself -- and the keyword grep flagged the prohibition as the violation.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.fixed_by: excluding any line carrying a prohibition/negation marker.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.lesson: third instance of negation-blindness inside this one card; same root as T1-24 Q-4 and T1-18 U-3.

error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.error: V-2 PASS was initially unproven: a criterion that never fires proves nothing by not firing.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.fixed_by: adding proposition V-2b, a self-test feeding the criterion synthetic signed-claims (must fire) and signing-vocabulary non-claims (must not fire): 5/5 and 7/7.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.lesson: a negative result from a criterion is only as strong as the criterion's demonstrated ability to return a positive.
